findings.message: The Scope in requires `phase5-continue-02` to embed "the merged `tests/test_seeded_phase5_01.py` continuation pattern". That file is new in this ticket's own admission (fence_facts: exists_on_main=false), so at seed authoring and requisition review it is neither merged nor existing on main. A Context entry naming it breaks the existing-path Context rule and the rule that new paths in the same admission are never Context. The established precedent does the same: `phase4-continue-05`, authored by `phase4-continue-04`, embeds `tests/test_seeded_phase4_03.py` and not its author's own new test. Section 20's 'immediately preceding merged seeded-test pattern' therefore means the most recent pattern already on main when the ticket is authored.
findings.paved_road: Have `phase5-continue-02` embed an already-merged seeded-test pattern (`tests/test_seeded_phase4_05.py`, this ticket's own Context) and pin its authoring-time size. List `tests/test_seeded_phase5_01.py` alongside the other paths new in this admission as excluded from the continuation's Context, and assert that exclusion in `tests/test_seeded_phase5_01.py`.

findings.message: The criteria pin 'authoring-time sizes' of the merged `squatch/retro.py` and `tests/test_retro.py`, but they do not forbid comparing those pins with live file sizes. `scorecard-reporting` fences and must edit both files, so any live-size comparison would turn this seeded test red as soon as that seed merges.
findings.paved_road: State in Scope in and the criteria that the authoring-time sizes are synthetic fixtures used only for the bounded max-effort render (the `_context`/`EXISTING_AT_AUTHORING` pattern in `tests/test_seeded_phase4_05.py`) and are never compared with later live file sizes.

findings.message: The criterion 'hard unique-bridge provenance lookup without a Merge-to-Box dependency' and the Definition of rejected entry 'Merge-owned Box' contradict merged behavior. `Merge.__init__` builds `self._box = Box(...)` (line 176) and passes it to `Verification(..., box=self._box)` in `_regate` (line 347) so that pre-existing base failures are filed as a `failure_report`. That Box is a production constructor. The criterion 'every production Box receives the callback' therefore reaches merge.py, while section 20 lists only the stage/runner/daemon/drain/serve/CLI constructors and says Merge never constructs a Box. The implementer can't meet both requirements unless they remove verification attribution's Box filing, which is out of scope.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket
